frontend.session.title: Session & navigation
frontend.session.purpose: Identifies the user and chooses a workspace.
frontend.session.note: Application roles come from the DEX account model. The login subject also identifies the trader's Ledger API user; it is not the party. The backend relays the trader token to register, prepare and execute. Ledger-user rights, Daml controllers and external-party signatures are separate authorization checks.

frontend.trader.title: Trader workspace
frontend.trader.purpose: Shows swaps for the trader's eligible pools.
frontend.trader.note: App.tsx composes the trader workspace from this swap desk, TraderOnboarding for access, LiquidityDesk for deposits and withdrawals, and Balances for holdings.

frontend.operator.title: Operator workspace
frontend.operator.purpose: Shows and runs settlement for one pool.
frontend.operator.note: OperatorSettlement selects the pool. The operator workspace also includes OperatorOnboardingDetail for access reviews and OperatorPools for pool proposals. App.tsx composes these screens. Real DVO decisions use the separate CLI.

frontend.wallet.title: Wallet bridge
frontend.wallet.purpose: Checks identity and asks the wallet to sign.
frontend.wallet.note: Topology signatures register the party. Transaction signatures authorize prepared ledger transactions. Private keys remain in the wallet.

frontend.data.title: API & live status
frontend.data.purpose: Adapts errors and refreshes visible status.
frontend.data.note: A logical grouping of UI helpers. It is not a separate service or a workflow engine.

client.reads.title: Account & catalogue
client.reads.purpose: Builds a typed client for account, catalogue and domain APIs.
client.reads.note: me, pools and activity expose profile, catalogue and caller-history reads. Onboarding, swaps, lp, tokens and admin are separate facets of the same client.

client.trader.title: Trader API
client.trader.purpose: Creates the liquidity API for deposits, withdrawals and positions.
client.trader.note: createDexClient composes lp, swaps and tokens as separate trading APIs. The swaps and tokens modules own their operations; all share the HTTP transport.

client.operator.title: Operator API
client.operator.purpose: Calls review, pool-proposal and settlement endpoints.

client.http.title: HTTP & errors
client.http.purpose: Sends typed requests and returns results or errors.
client.http.note: Stateless library transport. It does not sign, settle, poll, cache or retry requests.

backend.api.title: Fastify router
backend.api.purpose: Creates the Fastify HTTP entry point and request router.
backend.api.note: main.ts installs the IAM onRequest hook and registers each domain's routes.ts handlers. The server applies firewall rules, headers, body limits and error responses. Background workers call workflows without HTTP routing.

backend.application.title: Application wiring
backend.application.purpose: Composes the Fastify API, module dependencies and background workers.
backend.application.note: Registers authentication and domain routes. Workers run in this API process; Bootstrap and the DVO CLI are separate processes. Automatic settlement does not pass through HTTP routing.

backend.iam.title: IAM
backend.iam.purpose: Authenticates HTTP requests and resolves callers in Fastify's onRequest hook.
backend.iam.note: Verifies bearer tokens against the configured issuer. Application roles are stored in PostgreSQL. Account helpers query it through the shared database client, without a separate store. Fastify dispatches domain route handlers after this hook completes; IAM does not route requests to the business modules.

backend.activity.title: Activity
backend.activity.purpose: Combines the caller's stored swap and liquidity history.
backend.activity.note: PostgreSQL history comes through SwapStore and LiquidityStore. Filtered views delegate through each workflow's read-only activity() method; the combined view uses history ports. There are no ledger calls or trade execution. Individual request-status endpoints are separate.

backend.operations.title: Operations
backend.operations.purpose: Persists operator commands and coordinates SQL request queues.
backend.operations.note: The journal stores immutable submissions in PostgreSQL before dispatch. Queue helpers lock and order trader request admission and status updates. SettlementStore takes the shared pool lock itself and uses sequence helpers to return deferred requests to the queue tail.

backend.platform.title: Platform
backend.platform.purpose: Configures shared HTTP safeguards and error handling.
backend.platform.note: Platform also provides configuration in config.ts, database connections in database.ts and background loops in worker.ts. Domain rules stay in the business modules.

backend.onboarding.title: Onboarding
backend.onboarding.purpose: Connects approved accounts to parties and access.

backend.pools.title: Pools
backend.pools.purpose: Proposes pools and maintains their catalogue.

backend.swaps.title: Swaps
backend.swaps.purpose: Quotes and tracks signed swap requests.

backend.liquidity.title: Liquidity
backend.liquidity.purpose: Quotes and tracks deposits and LP withdrawals.

backend.settlements.title: Settlements
backend.settlements.purpose: Runs settlement batches through claim, preflight, dispatch, confirmation and recovery.
backend.settlements.note: Manual routes and the automatic loop start a run; SettlementStore applies the batch planner when it claims requests. Recovery resumes stored batches without selecting new requests. A PREPARING batch reruns preflight before its first submission or cancellation; confirmation and replay concern an immutable stored command.

backend.settlement-queues.title: Request queues
backend.settlement-queues.purpose: Reads and updates shared request rows, settlement policies and batch progress.
backend.settlement-queues.note: Swap, deposit and withdrawal queues are per pool and backed by PostgreSQL, not a message broker. Swaps and Liquidity assign queue order when submission begins; ledger confirmation makes requests eligible for settlement. SettlementStore reads and updates those same rows. Pool locks serialize admission, policy changes, claims and dispatch. Batch progress is persisted through the shared database client.

backend.settlement-decision.title: Batch planner
backend.settlement-decision.purpose: Selects settlement batches from per-pool queues and family policies.
backend.settlement-decision.note: SettlementWorkflow starts manual and automatic runs; SettlementStore.claim applies planning inside the pool-lock transaction. Automatic runs rotate enabled, unblocked families and wait for a full swap batch. Normal selection takes a FIFO prefix, skipping deferred requests and stopping at unconfirmed requests. A manual single-request selection may settle out of order.

backend.settlement-automation.title: Background loops
backend.settlement-automation.purpose: Runs automatic settlement and recovery in independent background loops.
backend.settlement-automation.note: Started by main.ts, both loops run inside the backend process and bypass HTTP routing. Automatic dispatch follows each pool family's policy; recovery continues even when automatic dispatch is disabled. Each loop starts immediately and waits three seconds after its previous pass before repeating. The same worker utility also drives domain request reconciliation.

backend.tokens.title: Tokens
backend.tokens.purpose: Reads balances and serves the development faucet.
backend.tokens.note: Reading token material from an adapter does not imply invoking this business workflow. The faucet is local development support.

backend.adapters.title: Canton client library
backend.adapters.purpose: Implements business ledger ports in the backend's internal Canton integration library.
backend.adapters.note: The Canton module contains domain adapters, interactive transactions, party setup and operator submissions. This shared ledger client supplies their JSON Ledger API IO. Token registry material comes from TokenRegistryStore rows in PostgreSQL.

backend.stores.title: Domain stores
backend.stores.purpose: Persists business records and request progress through the shared database client.
backend.stores.note: Onboarding, Pools, Swaps, Liquidity and Tokens each own their business records. Only SwapStore and LiquidityStore own settlement request rows and use admission helpers; SettlementStore reads and updates those same rows for settlement. A transaction that locks the pool queue row locks it before any request row.

backend.database-client.title: Database client
backend.database-client.purpose: Defines PostgreSQL table types, the connection pool and schema checks.
backend.database-client.note: Business workflows keep persistence in their module's store.ts. IAM account helpers and the Operations command journal also use this shared connection and table types.

contracts.access.title: Trader access
contracts.access.note: Current app onboarding grants access only to the pools approved in that review. Extending an existing trader to a later pool has no implemented app path. The DEX recovery wrapper requires current access/KYC; direct token withdrawal follows the issuer rules.

contracts.factory.title: Pool factory
contracts.factory.purpose: Validates proposals and creates pool state.
contracts.factory.note: The current development fixture creates the factory. The application proposes pools against an existing factory; it has no factory-creation flow.

contracts.proposal.title: Pool proposal
contracts.proposal.note: Conditional signatories: venueOperator always; settings.dvo only for an accepted proposal. Acceptance creates a successor then invokes the factory in the same transaction.

contracts.delegation.title: Settlement permission
contracts.delegation.purpose: DVO grants settlement authority for one pool.
contracts.delegation.note: Settlement combines trader-authorized allocations, this DVO grant and the operator controller. Revoking this grant moves no funds and does not erase trader allocations.

contracts.pool.title: Pool engine
contracts.pool.note: Pool rules verify the allocations bound to trader terms and the actual output limits. Token effects, receipts and state replacement commit together on-ledger; the prior request and application database are separate transactions.

contracts.state.title: Reserves & LP supply
contracts.state.purpose: Reserves, backing holdings and LP supply.

contracts.liquidity-receipt.title: Liquidity result
contracts.liquidity-receipt.purpose: Evidence of a deposit or redemption.

canton.ledger-api.title: Ledger API
canton.ledger-api.purpose: Receives reads, commands and signed submissions.

canton.party-hosting.title: Parties & hosting
canton.party-hosting.purpose: Registers parties and verifies local confirmation hosting.

canton.ledger-state.title: Ledger state & history
canton.ledger-state.purpose: Exposes contracts and confirmed transaction effects.
canton.ledger-state.note: Separate from the DEX PostgreSQL database. This is a participant capability, not a new DEX storage service.

canton.synchronizer.title: Global Synchronizer
canton.synchronizer.note: LocalNet uses its own synchronizer under the alias global. It does not connect to the public Global Synchronizer.

external.wallet.title: MetaMask + Canton Snap
external.wallet.purpose: MetaMask + Canton Snap is the trader's external wallet. It keeps private keys outside the app, signs Canton hashes and returns the signatures through this interface.

external.keycloak.title: Keycloak
external.keycloak.purpose: Keycloak is the identity provider for login. It issues the tokens that the configured participant accepts.
external.keycloak.note: Bootstrap configures this issuer on the participant. Trader operations and operator access reviews relay login tokens. Daml commands acting as the operator party and the DVO CLI use service credentials.

external.dvo.title: DVO
external.dvo.purpose: The DVO is the pool-authority party on Canton.
external.dvo.note: Approves or rejects pool proposals and grants the operator per-pool settlement authority. In LocalNet this alias resolves to a party hosted by the participant. The development CLI acts as that party; the CLI's PostgreSQL access is tooling, not a connection owned by a party.

external.token-standard.title: Token Standard
external.token-standard.purpose: Holdings, allocations and token settlement interfaces.
external.token-standard.note: Ledger interfaces implemented by issuers. They are not local DEX templates or an HTTP token service.

frontend.name: Frontend
frontend.purpose: People request actions and understand their outcomes.
frontend.short: Trader and operator workspaces · React + TypeScript
frontend.note: Wallet keys stay outside the application. The UI asks for a signature and sends it through the client.

client.name: Client
client.purpose: A small, typed vocabulary for calling the backend.
client.short: Typed HTTP APIs for the backend · TypeScript
client.boundary: Imported into the browser — no separate service
client.note: The client sends requests. It does not sign, price, settle or own background polling.

backend.name: Backend
backend.purpose: Durable business workflows, explicit settlement and ledger integration.
backend.short: HTTP API, workflows and persistence · TypeScript + Fastify + PostgreSQL
backend.boundary: Backend process, with a separate Canton network boundary
backend.note: Automatic settlement and recovery run as independent loops in the API process. Settlement boxes show logical responsibilities; request queues are backed by shared PostgreSQL tables. Canton client library is the internal canton/ integration package. Development setup tooling is omitted.

contracts.name: Contracts
contracts.purpose: Who may act, what can change, and which effects commit together.
contracts.short: Access, pools and settlement rules · Daml on Canton
contracts.boundary: DEX templates — executed by the Canton participant
contracts.note: DVO = pool authority. Operator = venueOperator. Trader = trader. Signatory, observer and controller are different roles.

canton.name: Canton
canton.purpose: Hosts parties, evaluates contracts and confirms ledger effects.
canton.note: Boxes show responsibilities. LocalNet configuration is the evidence baseline; no live deployment status is displayed.

overview.name: All Layers
overview.short: React UI → TypeScript client → Fastify backend → Daml contracts on Canton
